newsitem.title: USA: Blue chips lower after data but techs positive.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips lower after data but techs positive.

text.p: Stocks tumbled in very quiet pre-holiday trading Tuesday after reports of increased consumer confidence and strength in new home sales startled the markets and sparked fears of higher interest rates.
The Dow Jones industrial average was off 34.60 at 6,514.77 at 1 p.m. EST. On the broader market, decliners led gainers 6 to 5 on light New York Stock Exchange volume of 211 million shares.
All stock exchanges will be closed Wednesday for the New Year holiday.
Technology stocks bucked the trend and posted slight gains in a rebound from Monday's losses. The Nasdaq Composite Index rose 1.77 points to 1,289.52

"The consumer confidence numbers and the housing numbers were materially stronger than the Street had anticipated ... so this is a knee-jerk reaction by bonds and stocks," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer of Value Line's Asset Management division.

Investors were concerned that a stronger economy could increase chances that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates. In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell 1-1/4 points, or $12.50 per $1,000 face value, sending its yield up to 6.64 percent from 6.54 percent.

The Conference Board reported U.S. consumer confidence rose sharply in December to 113.8 vs. a revised 109.5 in November. At the same time, November new home sales exceeded economists' expectations and jumped 14.2 percent to 772,000, the steepest rise since April 1993.
The Chicago Purchasing Management Index for December was also stronger than expected, coming in at 57.4 compared with 57.6 last month and beating expectations for a reading of about 55.6.

Orlando said investors might be jittery for a few days after the robust data, awaiting more evidence on the direction of the economy. Wall Street is currently comfortable with its forecasts for a gradual slowing of the economy with no danger of any rise in interest rates.

Technology stocks rebounded slightly after Monday's losses. Compaq Computer Corp. rose 1-3/8 to 74-1/8 and Dell Computer Corp. added 1-3/4 to 54 after NatWest Securities raised its earnings forecasts for the companies.

"Millenium" software companies, which address data problems when computers switch into the year 2000, also rebounded from Monday's steep losses. Zitel Corp. rose 3 to 45-7/8 and Accelr8 Technology moved up 1-7/8 to 18-1/4.

Iomega Corp. shares lost 1/2 to 16 in heavy trading, after hitting a new low of 15-1/2. The maker of the Jaz and Zip disk drives said Monday it will take a $10 million pretax charge in the fourth quarter to shift more of its production to Asia, cutting up to 700 jobs at its Roy, Utah, facility.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks dropped 3.26 points to 750.59. The American Stock Exchange index fell 1.17 to 582.29.
